Shows parts of the coasts of Mexico, California, Oregon, Washington, and Alaska.

This collection contains 14 manuscript maps showing the Pacific Coast of North America from Mexico to the vicinity of Sitka, Alaska. The maps represent some of the first accurate Spanish charts of the west coast. Most were produced as a result of an expedition led by Bruno de Hezeta and Juan Francisco de la Bodega y Quadra, on behalf of New Spain and under the direction of Viceroy Antonio Bucareli y Ursua. The 14 maps range in size from 134 x 84 cm to 37 x 27 cm and typically show a stretch of coast, with some depicting toponyms, settlements, missions, fortifications, and soundings. Five of the charts attribute Hezeta as the creator, and six Bodega y Quadra. Four maps are cataloged separately. One of those maps is a 19th century manuscript copy of an earlier original map.
